Property management document processing system. Accepts uploaded files (PDF, CSV, EML, audio), classifies them against a Markdown-based property registry using LangChain and <NAME_1>, updates the relevant section in the property file, and exposes a natural-language query interface over the registry.

## How it works

```
File uploaded via <NAME_11>
        ↓
Text extracted & enqueued (immediate response)
  PDF  — text extracted in-memory via pypdf
  CSV  — each row enqueued as a separate item
  EML  — file saved to disk, parsed by worker
  Audio — file saved to disk, transcribed by worker via Gradium STT
        ↓
Worker picks up item
        ↓
RelevancyAgent — identifies property, building, unit, category
  └─ calls lookup_property_by_owner tool when owner name / email / IBAN
     appears instead of the property name
        ↓
ContentAgent — finds the matching section in the Markdown file and updates it
        ↓
Assessment stored in DB, result queryable via <NAME_11>
```

The property registry lives as Markdown files on the filesystem. The `QueryAgent` performs RAG over those files to answer natural-language questions about any property.

---

## Setup

**Requirements:** Python 3.11+, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)

```bash
# Install dependencies
uv sync

# Configure environment
cp .env.example .env
# Fill in at minimum GOOGLE_<NAME_11>_<NAME_14> (and GRADIUM_<NAME_11>_<NAME_14> if using audio)

# Start the <NAME_11> server (worker starts automatically)
uv run python main.py
```

---

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_<NAME_11>_<NAME_14>` | — | **Required.** <NAME_1> <NAME_11> key |
| `GRADIUM_<NAME_11>_<NAME_14>` | — | Required for audio transcription (speech-to-text) |
| `VENDOR_A_MODEL` | `<MODEL_A>` | <MODEL_A> model used by all agents |
| `repo34_PROPERTIES_DIR` | `data/properties` | Directory where property Markdown files are stored |
| `repo34_RUN_WORKER` | `true` | Set to `false` to disable the background worker on startup |
| `repo34_WORKER_BATCH_SIZE` | `10` | Queue items processed per worker batch |
| `repo34_WORKER_POLL_INTERVAL` | `5` | Seconds between worker queue polls |

---

## Property Markdown schema

Properties are stored as Markdown files in `repo34_PROPERTIES_DIR`. Each file follows this heading hierarchy:

```markdown
# Property Name

## owner
- Owner or management company name

## insurance
- Policy details

## maintanance
- Property-level maintenance notes

## buildings

### building 12
#### maintenance
#### rent

### building 16
#### maintenance
#### rent

#### units

##### unit WE 01
###### maintenance
###### rent
###### tenant

##### unit WE 02
...
```

Section content is a list of `- item` bullet points. Empty sections are valid placeholders.

---

## Owner database

Owners are stored in SQLite (`data/repo34_queue.db`) and used by the RelevancyAgent to match documents that reference a management company rather than the property name directly. The search matches on name, email address, or IBAN — and falls back to word-by-word matching when the full query has no result, so STT transcription variants (e.g. `"und"` instead of `"&"`) still resolve correctly.

```python
from owner_repository import OwnerRepository

repo = OwnerRepository()
repo.add(
    name="Huber & <NAME_5>",
    property_name="WEG Immanuelkirchstraße 26",
    street="Friedrichstrasse 112",
    postal_code="10117",
    city="<NAME_6>",
    email="<EMAIL_1>",
    phone="<PHONE_2>-0",
    iban="DE89 3704 <PHONE_3>",
    bic="<USER_6>",
    bank="<NAME_7>",
    tax_number="13/456/78901",
)
```

---

## <NAME_11> endpoints

### File upload

| Method | Path | Accepted formats | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/upload/pdf` | `.pdf` | Text extracted in-memory, one queue item |
| `POST` | `/upload/csv` | `.csv` | Each data row enqueued as a separate item |
| `POST` | `/upload/eml` | `.eml` | Email file saved to disk, parsed by worker |
| `POST` | `/upload/audio` | `.wav .mp3 .m4a .ogg .flac .webm` | Audio saved to disk, transcribed via Gradium STT |

All endpoints accept `multipart/form-data` with a single `file` field. No extra headers required.

**Single-file response (PDF / EML / audio):**
```json
{
  "status": "enqueued",
  "message": "invoice.pdf text extracted and enqueued",
  "data_id": "550e8400-...",
  "enqueued_at": "2026-01-01T10:00:00"
}
```

**CSV response** (one entry per row):
```json
{
  "status": "enqueued",
  "message": "data.csv parsed and 42 rows enqueued",
  "row_count": 42,
  "data_ids": ["abc-123", "def-456", "..."],
  "enqueued_at": "2026-01-01T10:00:00"
}
```

---

### Queue management

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/queue/status` | Counts by status (pending / processing / completed / failed) |
| `GET` | `/queue/item/{id}` | Details and assessment for a single item |
| `GET` | `/queue/completed?limit=100&hours=24` | Recently completed items |

Failed items are retried automatically up to **3 times** before being permanently marked as failed.

---

### Query (RAG)

```
POST /query
Content-Type: application/json

{ "prompt": "What is the maintenance schedule for building 16?" }
```

Response:
```json
{
  "answer": "The maintenance schedule for building 16 includes...",
  "sources": ["weg-immanuelkirchstrasse-26.md — WEG Immanuelkirchstraße 26 > buildings > building 16 > maintenance"]
}
```

The query agent parses all property files into heading-based sections, scores each section by relevance to the prompt (path matches weighted 3× over body matches), and feeds the top results to the LLM as grounded context.

---

### Adjustment history

```
GET /adjustments?limit=50
```

Returns the most recent content-agent updates — which section was changed, the original and updated content, and the action that triggered the change.

---

### Health check

```
GET /health
```

```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "agent_status": "ready",
  "query_agent_status": "ready",
  "worker_status": "running",
  "worker_stats": { "processed": 10, "completed": 9, "failed": 1, "errors": 1, "skipped": 0 }
}
```

---

## Agents

### RelevancyAgent

Reads uploaded document text and outputs:

```json
{
  "property": "WEG Immanuelkirchstraße 26",
  "building": null,
  "unit": "unit WE 49",
  "category": "maintenance",
  "action": "Invoice for janitorial services, garbage bin provision, and winter service."
}
```

- `property` — exact name from the Markdown registry (required)
- `building` — null when the document is property-level
- `unit` — null when not unit-specific
- `category` — one of `insurance | maintenance | rent | tenant`
- `action` — one or two sentence summary

When the property name is not in the document, the agent calls the `lookup_property_by_owner` tool, trying every name, email, and IBAN found in the document. For emails, all addresses from all header fields (From, To, CC, BCC, Reply-To, Sender) are collected and tried individually.

### ContentAgent

Takes the RelevancyAgent output, finds the matching section in the Markdown file, asks the LLM to update the content based on the action, and writes the result back to the file.

Section matching uses substring path matching with space-stripped fallback, so identifiers like `WE49` (from audio transcription) still match the heading `unit WE 49`. Property-level documents (no building or unit) prefer the shallowest matching section.

### QueryAgent

RAG pipeline over the property Markdown files:
1. Parses all files into `MarkdownSection` objects with heading paths and line numbers
2. Skips pure structural headings with no body content
3. Scores sections: path hits × 3 + body hits
4. Takes top 8 by score, re-sorts into document order for vendor_ent context
5. Passes formatted sections to <MODEL_A> with a system prompt that restricts the answer to the retrieved data

---

## Audio transcription

Audio files are transcribed via the [Gradium](https://gradium.ai) speech-to-text WebSocket <NAME_11> (`wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/asr`). The file is loaded, resampled to 24 kHz mono PCM, and streamed in 80 ms chunks. The transcript is then passed through the normal RelevancyAgent → ContentAgent pipeline.

**Supported formats:** WAV, MP3, M4A, OGG, FLAC, WebM

Requires `GRADIUM_<NAME_11>_<NAME_14>` in `.env`.

---

## Worker

The background worker runs inside the same process as the <NAME_11> server (controlled by `repo34_RUN_WORKER`). It can also be run standalone:

```bash
uv run python worker.py                           # continuous polling
uv run python worker.py --once                    # process one batch then exit
uv run python worker.py --stats                   # print queue stats then exit
uv run python worker.py --batch-size 20 --poll-interval 2
```

---

## Project structure

```
repo34/
├── main.py                  # Fast<NAME_11> app — upload, query, adjustments endpoints
├── worker.py                # Background queue worker
├── queue_manager.py         # SQLite queue (data/repo34_queue.db)
├── owner_repository.py      # SQLite owner → property index
├── audio_transcriber.py     # Gradium STT WebSocket client
├── agents/
│   ├── config.py            # Shared config (model, paths, <NAME_11> keys)
│   ├── relevancy_agent.py   # Document classifier with owner lookup tool
│   ├── content_agent.py     # Markdown section updater
│   └── query_agent.py       # RAG query agent
├── context_engine/
│   ├── engine.py            # ContextEngine — searches property files
│   ├── markdown_parser.py   # Parses heading-based Markdown into sections
│   └── models.py            # PropertyContext, BuildingContext, UnitContext
├── data/
│   ├── properties/          # Property Markdown files (repo34_PROPERTIES_DIR)
│   ├── uploads/
│   │   ├── eml/             # Saved EML files (worker reads these)
│   │   └── audio/           # Saved audio files (worker transcribes these)
│   ├── repo34_queue.db      # Queue + owner database
│   └── adjustments.db       # Content-agent update history
├── .env.example
└── pyproject.toml
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""vendor_c-agent-repo34 — vendor_c external agent plugin for the repo34 ContentAgent.

Discovered automatically by the <MODEL_C> CLI when placed on $PATH.
Communicates via JSON subcommands over stdin/stdout (protocol version 1).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import base64
import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Constants
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

AGENT_NAME = "repo34"
PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1
SESSION_SUBDIR = ".repo34/vendor_c-sessions"
HOOKS_CONFIG_PATH = ".repo34/hooks/entire.json"
TRANSCRIPT_EXT = ".jsonl"
HOOK_NAMES = ["session-start", "stop", "session-end"]


# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Required subcommands
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def cmd_info(_args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    _out({
        "protocol_version": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        "name": AGENT_NAME,
        "type": "repo34",
        "description": "repo34 ContentAgent — AI-powered property-management document editor",
        "is_preview": False,
        "protected_dirs": [".repo34"],
        "hook_names": HOOK_NAMES,
        "capabilities": {
            "hooks": True,
            "transcript_analyzer": True,
            "transcript_preparer": False,
            "token_calculator": False,
            "text_generator": False,
            "hook_response_writer": False,
            "subagent_aware_extractor": False,
        },
    })


def cmd_detect(_args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    try:
        import langchain_vendor_a  # noqa: F401
        present = True
    except ImportError:
        present = False
    _out({"present": present})


def cmd_get_session_id(_args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    hook_input = _read_stdin_json()
    _out({"session_id": hook_input["session_id"]})


def cmd_get_session_dir(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    session_dir = str(Path(args.repo_path) / SESSION_SUBDIR)
    _out({"session_dir": session_dir})


def cmd_resolve_session_file(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    session_file = str(Path(args.session_dir) / f"{args.session_id}{TRANSCRIPT_EXT}")
    _out({"session_file": session_file})


def cmd_read_session(_args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    hook_input = _read_stdin_json()
    session_id = hook_input.get("session_id", "")
    session_ref = hook_input.get("session_ref", "")
    repo_root = os.environ.get("ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT", "")

    native_data: str | None = None
    if session_ref:
        p = Path(session_ref)
        if p.exists():
            native_data = base64.b64encode(p.read_bytes()).decode()

    _out({
        "session_id": session_id,
        "agent_name": AGENT_NAME,
        "repo_path": repo_root,
        "session_ref": session_ref,
        "start_time": _now(),
        "native_data": native_data,
        "modified_files": [],
        "new_files": [],
        "deleted_files": [],
    })


def cmd_write_session(_args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    session = _read_stdin_json()
    session_ref = session.get("session_ref", "")
    native_data = session.get("native_data")
    if session_ref and native_data:
        path = Path(session_ref)
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_bytes(base64.b64decode(native_data))
    # Exit 0 on success (implicit)


def cmd_read_transcript(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    path = Path(args.session_ref)
    if path.exists():
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(path.read_bytes())


def cmd_chunk_transcript(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
    max_size = args.max_size
    chunks = [
        base64.b64encode(raw[i : i + max_size]).decode()
        for i in range(0, len(raw), max_size)
    ]
    _out({"chunks": chunks})


def cmd_reassemble_transcript(_args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    data = _read_stdin_json()
    for chunk_b64 in data.get("chunks", []):
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(base64.b64decode(chunk_b64))


def cmd_format_resume_command(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    _out({"command": f"repo34 --resume {args.session_id}"})


# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# hooks capability
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_HOOK_EVENT_TYPES: dict[str, int] = {
    "session-start": 1,
    "session_start": 1,
    "user_prompt_submit": 2,
    "stop": 3,
    "session-end": 5,
    "session_end": 5,
}


def cmd_parse_hook(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    hook_name = args.hook
    event_type = _HOOK_EVENT_TYPES.get(hook_name)
    if event_type is None:
        print("null")
        return

    hook_input = _read_stdin_json()
    event: dict = {
        "type": event_type,
        "session_id": hook_input.get("session_id", ""),
    }
    if hook_input.get("session_ref"):
        event["session_ref"] = hook_input["session_ref"]
    if hook_input.get("user_prompt"):
        event["prompt"] = hook_input["user_prompt"]
    if hook_input.get("timestamp"):
        event["timestamp"] = hook_input["timestamp"]
    else:
        event["timestamp"] = _now()
    _out(event)


def cmd_install_hooks(_args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    repo_root = Path(os.environ.get("ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT", "."))
    config_path = repo_root / HOOKS_CONFIG_PATH
    config_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    config_path.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "hooks": {
                    "session-start": {
                        "description": "Fired when a repo34 content-adjustment operation starts"
                    },
                    "stop": {
                        "description": "Fired when a repo34 content-adjustment turn completes"
                    },
                    "session-end": {
                        "description": "Fired when a repo34 session terminates"
                    },
                }
            },
            indent=2,
        )
    )
    _out({"hooks_installed": len(HOOK_NAMES)})


def cmd_uninstall_hooks(_args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    repo_root = Path(os.environ.get("ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT", "."))
    config_path = repo_root / HOOKS_CONFIG_PATH
    if config_path.exists():
        config_path.unlink()
    # Exit 0 on success (implicit)


def cmd_are_hooks_installed(_args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    repo_root = Path(os.environ.get("ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT", "."))
    config_path = repo_root / HOOKS_CONFIG_PATH
    _out({"installed": config_path.exists()})


# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# transcript_analyzer capability
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def cmd_get_transcript_position(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    path = Path(args.path)
    pos = path.stat().st_size if path.exists() else 0
    _out({"position": pos})


def cmd_extract_modified_files(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Parse the session JSONL from *offset* to find files written by ContentAgent."""
    path = Path(args.path)
    offset = args.offset
    modified: list[str] = []
    current_position = offset

    if path.exists():
        raw = path.read_bytes()
        current_position = len(raw)
        chunk = raw[offset:].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        for line in chunk.splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                entry = json.loads(line)
                # ContentAgent.adjust() returns {"markdown_path": "...", "updated": true, ...}
                if entry.get("updated") and entry.get("markdown_path"):
                    rel = entry["markdown_path"]
                    if rel not in modified:
                        modified.append(rel)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                pass

    _out({"files": modified, "current_position": current_position})


# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Helpers
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _out(data: object) -> None:
    print(json.dumps(data), flush=True)


def _read_stdin_json() -> dict:
    return json.loads(sys.stdin.read())


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CLI entry-point
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="vendor_c-agent-repo34",
        description="vendor_c external agent plugin for repo34 ContentAgent",
    )
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")

    # ── required ──────────────────────────────────────────
    sub.add_parser("info")
    sub.add_parser("detect")
    sub.add_parser("get-session-id")

    p = sub.add_parser("get-session-dir")
    p.add_argument("--repo-path", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("resolve-session-file")
    p.add_argument("--session-dir", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--session-id", required=True)

    sub.add_parser("read-session")
    sub.add_parser("write-session")

    p = sub.add_parser("read-transcript")
    p.add_argument("--session-ref", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("chunk-transcript")
    p.add_argument("--max-size", type=int, required=True)

    sub.add_parser("reassemble-transcript")

    p = sub.add_parser("format-resume-command")
    p.add_argument("--session-id", required=True)

    # ── hooks capability ──────────────────────────────────
    p = sub.add_parser("parse-hook")
    p.add_argument("--hook", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("install-hooks")
    p.add_argument("--local-dev", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--force", action="store_true")

    sub.add_parser("uninstall-hooks")
    sub.add_parser("are-hooks-installed")

    # ── transcript_analyzer capability ────────────────────
    p = sub.add_parser("get-transcript-position")
    p.add_argument("--path", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("extract-modified-files")
    p.add_argument("--path", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--offset", type=int, default=0)

    args = parser.parse_args()

    dispatch = {
        "info": cmd_info,
        "detect": cmd_detect,
        "get-session-id": cmd_get_session_id,
        "get-session-dir": cmd_get_session_dir,
        "resolve-session-file": cmd_resolve_session_file,
        "read-session": cmd_read_session,
        "write-session": cmd_write_session,
        "read-transcript": cmd_read_transcript,
        "chunk-transcript": cmd_chunk_transcript,
        "reassemble-transcript": cmd_reassemble_transcript,
        "format-resume-command": cmd_format_resume_command,
        "parse-hook": cmd_parse_hook,
        "install-hooks": cmd_install_hooks,
        "uninstall-hooks": cmd_uninstall_hooks,
        "are-hooks-installed": cmd_are_hooks_installed,
        "get-transcript-position": cmd_get_transcript_position,
        "extract-modified-files": cmd_extract_modified_files,
    }

    if args.command not in dispatch:
        parser.print_help(sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    try:
        dispatch[args.command](args)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"vendor_c-agent-repo34: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

### vendor_c-agent-repo34

`vendor_c-agent-repo34` is a custom Entire external agent plugin that connects the repo34 `ContentAgent` to the <MODEL_C> checkpoint system. It is a Python script that must be placed on `$PATH` so the <MODEL_C> CLI can discover and invoke it automatically.

- Fires three hook events tied to `ContentAgent` operations:

  - `stop` — when an adjustment turn completes
  - `session-end` — when the session terminates
- Stores session transcripts as JSONL files in `.repo34/vendor_c-sessions/`

def normalize(v):
    return ' '.join(str(v).casefold().strip().strip(':').split())

def find_section(sections, prop, bldg, unit, cat):
    np_, nb, nu, nc = normalize(prop), normalize(bldg), normalize(unit), normalize(cat)
    candidates = []
    for s in sections:
        pn = [normalize(x) for x in s.path]
        if nc and pn[-1] != nc: continue
        if nu and not any(nu in p or nu.replace(' ','') in p.replace(' ','') for p in pn): continue
        if nb and not any(nb in p or nb.replace(' ','') in p.replace(' ','') for p in pn): continue
        if np_ and (not pn or pn[0] != np_): continue
        candidates.append(s)
    if not candidates: return None
    if not nb and not nu:
        candidates.sort(key=lambda s: len(s.path))
    return candidates[0]

Everything is correct now. To summarise what was happening and the current state:

**Root cause** — the property-level heading was spelled `## maintanance` (typo). `_find_section` does exact matching on the last path element, so `"maintanance" ≠ "maintenance"` caused the property-level section to be skipped. The shallowest remaining match was `#### maintenance` under building 12, so every property-wide maintenance document landed there.

**Current state** — the file now has `## maintenance` (corrected), the full hierarchy is clean:

| Depth | Sections |
|---|---|
| 2 | `owner`, `insurance`, `maintenance`, `buildings` |
| 3 | `building 12`, `building 14`, `building 16` |
| 4 | `maintenance`, `rent`, `units` (per building) |
| 5 | `unit WE 01` … `unit TG 52` |
| 6 | `maintenance`, `rent`, `tenant` (per unit) |

**Routing is now correct:**
- Property-level maintenance doc → `WEG … > maintenance` ✓
- Building 12 doc → `WEG … > buildings > building 12 > maintenance` ✓
- Unit WE 49 tenant doc → `… > unit WE 49 > tenant` ✓
- Insurance doc → `WEG … > insurance` ✓

1	"""Worker process for processing queued webhook data.
2	
3	This module runs continuously, fetching items from the queue and running
4	them through the relevancy agent's agentic workflow.
5	
6	<NAME_13>:
7	    python worker.py
8	"""
9	
10	import json
11	import argparse
12	import csv
13	from email import policy
14	from email.parser import BytesParser
15	import logging
16	import signal
17	import time
18	import threading
19	from pathlib import Path
20	from io import StringIO
21	
22	from queue_manager import QueueManager, DataSource
23	
24	
25	# Configure logging
26	logging.basicConfig(
27	    level=logging.INFO,
28	    format="%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s",
29	)
30	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
31	
32	
33	class QueueWorker:
34	    """Worker that processes items from the queue."""
35	
36	    def __init__(
37	        self,
38	        batch_size: int = 10,
39	        poll_interval: int = 5,
40	        initialize_agent: bool = True,
41	        agent=None,
42	    ):
43	        """Initialize worker.
44	
45	        Args:
46	            batch_size: Number of items to process per batch
47	            poll_interval: Seconds to wait between polls
48	            initialize_agent: Whether to initialize the relevancy agent
49	            agent: Existing relevancy agent instance to reuse
50	        """
51	        self.batch_size = batch_size
52	        self.poll_interval = poll_interval
53	        self.queue_manager = QueueManager()
54	        self.stop_event = threading.Event()
55	
56	        if agent is not None:
57	            self.agent = agent
58	            logger.info("✓ Reusing existing relevancy agent")
59	        elif initialize_agent:
60	            try:
61	                from agents.relevancy_agent import RelevancyAgent
62	
63	                self.agent = RelevancyAgent()
64	                logger.info("✓ Relevancy agent initialized")
65	            except ValueError as e:
66	                logger.error(f"✗ Failed to initialize agent: {e}")
67	                self.agent = None
68	        else:
69	            self.agent = None
70	
71	        self.running = True
72	        self.stats = {
73	            "processed": 0,
74	            "completed": 0,
75	            "failed": 0,
76	            "errors": 0,
77	            "skipped": 0,
78	        }
79	
80	    def format_webhook_data(self, source: str, payload: dict) -> str:
81	        """Convert webhook data to text for agent evaluation.
82	
83	        Args:
84	            source: Data source (email, slack, erp)
85	            payload: Raw webhook payload
86	
87	        Returns:
88	            Formatted text for agent
89	        """
90	        try:
91	            if source == DataSource.PDF_INVOICE.value:
92	                return self.parse_pdf_invoice_upload(payload)
93	
94	            elif source == DataSource.CSV.value:
95	                return self.parse_csv_upload(payload)
96	
97	            elif source == DataSource.EML.value:
98	                return self.parse_eml_upload(payload)
99	
100	            else:
101	                logger.warning(f"Unknown source: {source}")
102	                return json.dumps(payload)
103	
104	        except Exception as e:
105	            logger.error(f"Error formatting webhook data: {e}")
106	            return json.dumps(payload)
107	
108	    def parse_pdf_invoice_upload(self, payload: dict) -> str:
109	        """Extract text from an uploaded invoice PDF task."""
110	        file_path = self._get_upload_path(payload)
111	        try:
112	            from pypdf import PdfReader
113	        except ImportError as exc:
114	            raise RuntimeError(
115	                "PDF processing requires the pypdf package. Install it before processing invoice PDFs."
116	            ) from exc
117	
118	        reader = PdfReader(str(file_path))
119	        page_text = []
120	        for page_number, page in enumerate(reader.pages, start=1):
121	            text = page.extract_text() or ""
122	            page_text.append(f"--- Page {page_number} ---\n{text.strip()}")
123	
124	        return self._format_uploaded_document(
125	            "INVOICE PDF",
126	            payload,
127	            "\n\n".join(page_text).strip() or "[No extractable PDF text found]",
128	        )
129	
130	    def parse_csv_upload(self, payload: dict) -> str:
131	        """Parse an uploaded CSV task into text for the agent."""
132	        file_path = self._get_upload_path(payload)
133	        raw_text = file_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
134	        reader = csv.DictReader(StringIO(raw_text))
135	
136	        if reader.fieldnames:
137	            rows = []
138	            for row_number, row in enumerate(reader, start=1):
139	                values = ", ".join(f"{key}: {value}" for key, value in row.items())
140	                rows.append(f"Row {row_number}: {values}")
141	            content = f"Columns: {', '.join(reader.fieldnames)}\n" + "\n".join(rows)
142	        else:
143	            content = raw_text
144	
145	        return self._format_uploaded_document("CSV FILE", payload, content.strip())
146	
147	    def parse_eml_upload(self, payload: dict) -> str:
148	        """Parse an uploaded .eml task into text for the agent."""
149	        file_path = self._get_upload_path(payload)
150	        message = BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(file_path.read_bytes())
151	
152	        body = message.get_body(preferencelist=("plain", "html"))
153	        body_text = body.get_content() if body else ""
154	        attachments = [
155	            part.get_filename()
156	            for part in message.iter_attachments()
157	            if part.get_filename()
158	        ]
159	
160	        content = "\n".join(
161	            [
162	                f"From: {message.get('from', 'Unknown')}",
163	                f"To: {message.get('to', 'Unknown')}",
164	                f"Subject: {message.get('subject', '')}",
165	                f"Date: {message.get('date', '')}",
166	                f"Attachments: {', '.join(attachments) if attachments else 'None'}",
167	                "",
168	                body_text.strip(),
169	            ]
170	        )
171	        return self._format_uploaded_document("EMAIL FILE", payload, content.strip())
172	
173	    def _get_upload_path(self, payload: dict) -> Path:
174	        """Get and validate the uploaded file path from a queued task."""
175	        file_path = Path(payload["file_path"])
176	        if not file_path.exists():
177	            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Queued upload file not found: {file_path}")
178	        return file_path
179	
180	    def _format_uploaded_document(self, label: str, payload: dict, content: str) -> str:
181	        """Format uploaded file content for agent evaluation."""
182	        return content
183	
184	    def process_item(self, item: dict) -> bool:
185	        """Process a single queue item.
186	
187	        Args:
188	            item: Queue item from database
189	
190	        Returns:
191	            True if processing was successful, False otherwise
192	        """
193	        item_id = item["id"]
194	        source = item["source"]
195	
196	        try:
197	            if not self.agent:
198	                raise ValueError("Agent not initialized")
199	
200	            # Atomically claim the item so multiple worker processes can run safely.
201	            if not self.queue_manager.set_processing(item_id):
202	                logger.info(f"Skipping already-claimed item: {item_id}")
203	                self.stats["skipped"] += 1
204	                return False
205	
206	            # Parse payload
207	            payload = json.loads(item["payload"])
208	            text_to_evaluate = self.format_webhook_data(source, payload)
209	
210	            logger.info(f"Processing {source} item: {item_id}")
211	
212	            # Run agent evaluation
213	            result = self.agent.evaluate(text_to_evaluate)
214	            assessment = json.dumps(result["assessment"])
215	
216	            # Mark as completed
217	            self.queue_manager.mark_completed(item_id, assessment)
218	
219	            logger.info(f"✓ Completed: {item_id}")
220	            self.stats["completed"] += 1
221	
222	            return True
223	
224	        except Exception as e:
225	            logger.error(f"✗ Error processing {item_id}: {e}")
226	            self.queue_manager.mark_failed(item_id, str(e), retry=True)
227	            self.stats["errors"] += 1
228	            return False
229	
230	    def process_batch(self) -> int:
231	        """Process a batch of pending items.
232	
233	        Returns:
234	            Number of items processed
235	        """
236	        items = self.queue_manager.get_pending_items(limit=self.batch_size)
237	
238	        if not items:
239	            return 0
240	
241	        logger.info(f"Processing batch of {len(items)} items...")
242	
243	        processed = 0
244	        for item in items:
245	            if self.process_item(item):
246	                processed += 1
247	            self.stats["processed"] += 1
248	
249	        return processed
250	
251	    def print_stats(self):
252	        """Print worker statistics."""
253	        queue_stats = self.queue_manager.get_queue_stats()
254	        logger.info(f"Queue Stats: {queue_stats}")
255	        logger.info(f"Worker Stats: {self.stats}")
256	
257	    def run_once(self) -> int:
258	        """Run a single scheduled processing tick.
259	
260	        Returns:
261	            Number of items successfully processed
262	        """
263	        if not self.agent:
264	            logger.error("Cannot process queue: agent not initialized")
265	            return 0
266	
267	        processed = self.process_batch()
268	
269	        if processed > 0:
270	            logger.info(f"Batch complete. Processed {processed} items.")
271	            self.print_stats()
272	
273	        return processed
274	
275	    def run(self):
276	        """Run worker on a periodic schedule until stopped."""
277	        if not self.agent:
278	            logger.error("Cannot start worker: agent not initialized")
279	            return
280	
281	        logger.info(
282	            "Starting worker scheduler "
283	            f"(batch_size={self.batch_size}, interval={self.poll_interval}s)"
284	        )
285	        logger.info("Press Ctrl+C to stop")
286	
287	        try:
288	            next_run = time.monotonic()
289	            while self.running and not self.stop_event.is_set():
290	                now = time.monotonic()
291	                wait_seconds = max(0, next_run - now)
292	                if self.stop_event.wait(wait_seconds):
293	                    break
294	
295	                started_at = time.monotonic()
296	                self.run_once()
297	                next_run = max(next_run + self.poll_interval, started_at + self.poll_interval)
298	
299	        except KeyboardInterrupt:
300	            logger.info("Stopping worker...")
301	            self.running = False
302	        except Exception as e:
303	            logger.error(f"Worker error: {e}")
304	            self.running = False
305	
306	        self.print_stats()
307	        logger.info("Worker stopped")
308	
309	    def signal_handler(self, sig, frame):
310	        """Handle shutdown signals."""
311	        logger.info("Received shutdown signal")
312	        self.running = False
313	        self.stop_event.set()
314

18

20	@dataclass
21	class _OutlineNode:
22	    """Small indentation outline node used for property context Markdown."""
23	
24	    key: str
25	    value: str = ""
26	    indent: int = 0
27	    line_number: int = 0
28	    children: list["_OutlineNode"] = field(default_factory=list)

31	@dataclass
32	class _HeadingNode:
33	    """Markdown heading node used for property context Markdown."""
34	
35	    title: str
36	    level: int
37	    line_number: int = 0
38	    content: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

42	class MarkdownParser:
43	    """Parse property Markdown documents."""
44	
45	    def parse_file(self, markdown_path: str | Path) -> list[MarkdownSection]:
46	        """Parse a Markdown file into sections."""
47	        path = Path(markdown_path)
48	        return self.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
49	
50	    def parse_property_file(self, markdown_path: str | Path) -> PropertyContext:
51	        """Parse one property Markdown file into structured property context."""
52	        path = Path(markdown_path)
53	        property_context = self.parse_property(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
54	        property_context.markdown_path = str(path)
55	        return property_context
56	
57	    def parse_property(self, markdown: str) -> PropertyContext:
58	        """Parse the heading-based property Markdown format.
59	
60	        Expected shape:
61	
62	        # property
63	        ## insurance
64	        ## maintanance
65	        ## buildings:
66	        ### haus1
67	        #### maintenance
68	        #### rent
69	        #### units:
70	        ##### aprt1
71	        ###### maintenance
72	        ###### rent
73	        ###### tenant
74	        """
75	        root = self._parse_heading_tree(markdown)
76	        property_node = self._first_heading(root, level=1)
77	        if property_node is None:
78	            raise ValueError("Property Markdown must start with a level 1 property heading")
79	
80	        property_context = PropertyContext(name=self._clean_heading(property_node.title))
81	        self._apply_property_heading_children(property_context, property_node.children)
82	        return property_context
83	
84	    def parse(self, markdown: str) -> list[MarkdownSection]:
85	        """Parse Markdown content into heading-based sections."""
86	        lines = markdown.splitlines()
87	        sections: list[MarkdownSection] = []
88	        stack: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
89	        current_title = "Document"
90	        current_level = 0
91	        current_start = 1
92	        current_content: list[str] = []
93	        current_path: list[str] = []
94	
95	        line_index = 0
96	        if lines and lines[0].strip() == "---":
97	            closing_index = self._find_front_matter_end(lines)
98	            if closing_index is not None:
99	                front_matter = "\n".join(lines[1:closing_index])
100	                sections.append(
101	                    MarkdownSection(
102	                        title="Front Matter",
103	                        level=0,
104	                        content=front_matter,
105	                        start_line=1,
106	                        end_line=closing_index + 1,
107	                        path=["Front Matter"],
108	                        section_type="front_matter",
109	                    )
110	                )
111	                line_index = closing_index + 1
112	                current_start = line_index + 1
113	
114	        while line_index < len(lines):
115	            line = lines[line_index]
116	            heading_match = HEADING_RE.match(line)
117	
118	            if heading_match:
119	                if current_content or current_title != "Document":
120	                    sections.append(
121	                        MarkdownSection(
122	                            title=current_title,
123	                            level=current_level,
124	                            content="\n".join(current_content).strip(),
125	                            start_line=current_start,
126	                            end_line=line_index,
127	                            path=current_path or [current_title],
128	                        )
129	                    )
130	
131	                current_level = len(heading_match.group(1))
132	                current_title = heading_match.group(2).strip()
133	                stack = [item for item in stack if item[0] < current_level]
134	                stack.append((current_level, current_title))
135	                current_path = [title for _, title in stack]
136	                current_start = line_index + 1
137	                current_content = [line]
138	            else:
139	                current_content.append(line)
140	
141	            line_index += 1
142	
143	        if current_content or not sections:
144	            sections.append(
145	                MarkdownSection(
146	                    title=current_title,
147	                    level=current_level,
148	                    content="\n".join(current_content).strip(),
149	                    start_line=current_start,
150	                    end_line=len(lines),
151	                    path=current_path or [current_title],
152	                )
153	            )
154	
155	        return [
156	            section
157	            for section in sections
158	            if section.content or section.section_type == "front_matter"
159	        ]
160	
161	    def _find_front_matter_end(self, lines: list[str]) -> int | None:
162	        """Return the closing line index for YAML-style front matter."""
163	        for index in range(1, len(lines)):
164	            if lines[index].strip() == "---":
165	                return index
166	        return None
167	
168	    def _parse_heading_tree(self, markdown: str) -> _HeadingNode:
169	        """Parse Markdown headings and their content into a tree."""
170	        root = _HeadingNode(title="Document", level=0)
171	        stack: list[_HeadingNode] = [root]
172	
173	        for line_number, line in enumerate(markdown.splitlines(), start=1):
174	            heading_match = HEADING_RE.match(line)
175	            if heading_match:
176	                level = len(heading_match.group(1))
177	                node = _HeadingNode(
178	                    title=heading_match.group(2).strip(),
179	                    level=level,
180	                    line_number=line_number,
181	                )
182	                while stack and level <= stack[-1].level:
183	                    stack.pop()
184	                stack[-1].children.append(node)
185	                stack.append(node)
186	            elif stack:
187	                stack[-1].content.append(line)
188	
189	        return root
190	
191	    def _first_heading(
192	        self,
193	        root: _HeadingNode,
194	        level: int,
195	    ) -> _HeadingNode | None:
196	        """Return the first heading at the requested level."""
197	        for child in root.children:
198	            if child.level == level:
199	                return child
200	        return None
201	
202	    def _apply_property_heading_children(
203	        self,
204	        property_context: PropertyContext,
205	        children: list[_HeadingNode],
206	    ) -> None:
207	        for child in children:
208	            normalized_key = self._normalize_key(child.title)
209	
210	            if normalized_key == "insurance":
211	                property_context.insurance = self._section_items(child)
212	            elif normalized_key in {"maintenance", "maintanance"}:
213	                property_context.maintenance = self._section_items(child)
214	            elif normalized_key == "buildings":
215	                property_context.buildings.extend(
216	                    self._parse_building_heading(node) for node in child.children
217	                )
218	            else:
219	                property_context.attributes[child.title] = self._section_items(child)
220	
221	    def _parse_building_heading(self, node: _HeadingNode) -> PropertyBuildingContext:
222	        building = PropertyBuildingContext(name=self._clean_heading(node.title))
223	        for child in node.children:
224	            normalized_key = self._normalize_key(child.title)
225	
226	            if normalized_key in {"maintenance", "maintanance"}:
227	                building.maintenance = self._section_items(child)
228	            elif normalized_key == "rent":
229	                building.rent = self._section_items(child)
230	            elif normalized_key == "units":
231	                building.units.extend(
232	                    self._parse_unit_heading(unit) for unit in child.children
233	                )
234	            else:
235	                building.attributes[child.title] = self._section_items(child)
236	
237	        return building
238	
239	    def _parse_unit_heading(self, node: _HeadingNode) -> PropertyUnitContext:
240	        unit = PropertyUnitContext(name=self._clean_heading(node.title))
241	        for child in node.children:
242	            normalized_key = self._normalize_key(child.title)
243	
244	            if normalized_key in {"maintenance", "maintanance"}:
245	                unit.maintenance = self._section_items(child)
246	            elif normalized_key == "rent":
247	                unit.rent = self._section_items(child)
248	            elif normalized_key == "tenant":
249	                unit.tenant = "\n".join(self._section_items(child)).strip()
250	            else:
251	                unit.attributes[child.title] = self._section_items(child)
252	
253	        return unit
254	
255	    def _section_items(self, node: _HeadingNode) -> list[str]:
256	        """Return cleaned non-empty lines under a heading as list items."""
257	        items: list[str] = []
258	        for line in node.content:
259	            stripped = line.strip()
260	            if not stripped:
261	                continue
262	            if stripped.startswith("- "):
263	                stripped = stripped[2:].strip()
264	            items.append(stripped)
265	        return items
266	
267	    def _parse_outline(self, markdown: str) -> _OutlineNode:
268	        """Parse indented Markdown/list lines into a shallow outline tree."""
269	        root = _OutlineNode(key="Document", indent=-1)
270	        stack: list[_OutlineNode] = [root]
271	
272	        for line_number, raw_line in enumerate(markdown.splitlines(), start=1):
273	            if not raw_line.strip() or raw_line.strip() == "---":
274	                continue
275	
276	            indent = len(raw_line.expandtabs(4)) - len(raw_line.expandtabs(4).lstrip())
277	            key, value = self._split_outline_line(raw_line.strip())
278	            if not key:
279	                continue
280	
281	            node = _OutlineNode(
282	                key=key,
283	                value=value,
284	                indent=indent,
285	                line_number=line_number,
286	            )
287	            while stack and indent <= stack[-1].indent:
288	                stack.pop()
289	            stack[-1].children.append(node)
290	            stack.append(node)
291	
292	        return root
293	
294	    def _split_outline_line(self, stripped_line: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
295	        """Split an outline line into key/value parts."""
296	        line = stripped_line
297	        if line.startswith("- "):
298	            line = line[2:].strip()
299	
300	        heading_match = HEADING_RE.match(line)
301	        if heading_match:
302	            line = heading_match.group(2).strip()
303	
304	        if ":" not in line:
305	            return line.strip(), ""
306	
307	        key, value = line.split(":", 1)
308	        return key.strip(), value.strip()
309	
310	    def _first_content_node(self, root: _OutlineNode) -> _OutlineNode | None:
311	        """Return the first non-front-matter node."""
312	        for node in root.children:
313	            if node.key.lower() not in {"front matter", "metadata"}:
314	                return node
315	        return None
316	
317	    def _apply_property_children(
318	        self,
319	        property_context: PropertyContext,
320	        children: list[_OutlineNode],
321	    ) -> None:
322	        for child in children:
323	            normalized_key = self._normalize_key(child.key)
324	            value = self._node_value(child)
325	
326	            if normalized_key == "insurance":
327	                property_context.insurance = value
328	            elif normalized_key in {"maintenance", "maintanance"}:
329	                property_context.maintenance = value
330	            elif normalized_key == "buildings":
331	                property_context.buildings.extend(
332	                    self._parse_building_node(node) for node in child.children
333	                )
334	            else:
335	                property_context.attributes[child.key] = value
336	
337	    def _parse_building_node(self, node: _OutlineNode) -> PropertyBuildingContext:
338	        building = PropertyBuildingContext(name=self._clean_heading(node.key))
339	        for child in node.children:
340	            normalized_key = self._normalize_key(child.key)
341	            value = self._node_value(child)
342	
343	            if normalized_key in {"maintenance", "maintanance"}:
344	                building.maintenance = value
345	            elif normalized_key == "rent":
346	                building.rent = value
347	            elif normalized_key == "units":
348	                building.units.extend(
349	                    self._parse_unit_node(unit) for unit in child.children
350	                )
351	            else:
352	                building.attributes[child.key] = value
353	
354	        return building
355	
356	    def _parse_unit_node(self, node: _OutlineNode) -> PropertyUnitContext:
357	        unit = PropertyUnitContext(name=self._clean_heading(node.key))
358	        for child in node.children:
359	            normalized_key = self._normalize_key(child.key)
360	            value = self._node_value(child)
361	
362	            if normalized_key in {"maintenance", "maintanance"}:
363	                unit.maintenance = value
364	            elif normalized_key == "rent":
365	                unit.rent = value
366	            elif normalized_key == "tenant":
367	                unit.tenant = value
368	            else:
369	                unit.attributes[child.key] = value
370	
371	        return unit
372	
373	    def _node_value(self, node: _OutlineNode) -> str:
374	        """Return a node's inline value or text represented by child leaf nodes."""
375	        if node.value:
376	            return node.value
377	
378	        leaf_values = [
379	            child.value or child.key
380	            for child in node.children
381	            if not child.children
382	        ]
383	        return "\n".join(leaf_values).strip()
384	
385	    def _normalize_key(self, key: str) -> str:
386	        """Normalize outline keys for matching."""
387	        return self._clean_heading(key).lower().replace(" ", "_")
388	
389	    def _clean_heading(self, value: str) -> str:
390	        """Clean Markdown/list syntax from a heading-like value."""
391	        return value.strip().strip(":").strip()

11	    PropertyUnitContext,

15	class ContextEngine:
16	    """Load property context directly from Markdown files in a repo."""
17	
18	    def __init__(
19	        self,
20	        repo_path: str | Path = ".",
21	        property_glob: str = "**/*.md",
22	    ):
23	        """Initialize the context engine.
24	
25	        Args:
26	            repo_path: Git repo or filesystem root that contains property files.
27	            property_glob: Glob used to discover property Markdown files.
28	        """
29	        self.repo_path = Path(repo_path)
30	        self.property_glob = property_glob
31	        self.parser = MarkdownParser()
32	
33	    def list_properties(self) -> list[PropertyContext]:
34	        """Load all parseable property Markdown files under the repo path."""
35	        properties: list[PropertyContext] = []
36	        for markdown_path in self._iter_markdown_files():
37	            try:
38	                properties.append(self.parser.parse_property_file(markdown_path))
39	            except ValueError:
40	                continue
41	
42	        return properties
43	
44	    def get_property(self, property_name: str) -> PropertyContext | None:
45	        """Find a property by <USER_2>"""
46	        normalized_name = self._normalize(property_name)
47	        for property_context in self.list_properties():
48	            if self._normalize(property_context.name) == normalized_name:
49	                return property_context
50	
51	        return None
52	
53	    def find_properties(self, query: str, limit: int = 20) -> list[PropertyContext]:
54	        """Find properties by property, building, unit, or attribute text."""
55	        normalized_query = self._normalize(query)
56	        matches = [
57	            property_context
58	            for property_context in self.list_properties()
59	            if normalized_query
60	            in self._normalize(self._property_search_text(property_context))
61	        ]
62	        return matches[:limit]
63	
64	    def find_buildings(
65	        self,
66	        query: str,
67	        property_name: str | None = None,
68	        limit: int = 20,
69	    ) -> list[PropertyBuildingContext]:
70	        """Find buildings by name or content."""
71	        normalized_query = self._normalize(query)
72	        matches: list[PropertyBuildingContext] = []
73	
74	        for property_context in self._properties_for_scope(property_name):
75	            for building in property_context.buildings:
76	                if normalized_query in self._normalize(
77	                    self._building_search_text(building)
78	                ):
79	                    matches.append(building)
80	                    if len(matches) >= limit:
81	                        return matches

import os

from typing import Any

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from langchain_vendor_a import ChatGooglevendor_a
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate

from context_engine.engine import ContextEngine
from context_engine.markdown_parser import MarkdownParser
from context_engine.models import MarkdownSection

load_dotenv()


class ContentAgent:
    """Agent that adjusts a Markdown property-file section based on an action."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        api_key: str | None = None,
        repo_path: str | Path = ".",
    ):
        if api_key is None:
            api_key = os.getenv("GOOGLE_<NAME_11>_<NAME_14>")
            if not api_key:
                raise ValueError(
                    "GOOGLE_<NAME_11>_<NAME_14> environment variable not set. "
                    "Please set it or pass api_key parameter."
                )

        self.llm = ChatGooglevendor_a(
            model="<MODEL_A>",
            google_api_key=api_key,
            temperature=0.3,
        )
        self.parser = MarkdownParser()
        self.engine = ContextEngine(repo_path=repo_path)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public <NAME_11>
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def adjust(
        self,
        relevancy_output: dict[str, Any],
        markdown_path: str | Path | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Adjust the section described by *relevancy_output* inside a Markdown file.

        Args:
            relevancy_output: Dict produced by RelevancyAgent with keys
                property, building, unit, category, action.
            markdown_path: Explicit path to the Markdown file.  When omitted
                the ContextEngine searches by property name under repo_path.

        Returns:
            Dict with updated, section_path, original_content, adjusted_content.
        """
        property_name = relevancy_output.get("property", "")
        building_name = relevancy_output.get("building", "")
        unit_name = relevancy_output.get("unit", "")
        category = relevancy_output.get("category", "")
        action = relevancy_output.get("action", "")

        path = self._resolve_markdown_path(markdown_path, property_name)

        sections = self.parser.parse_file(path)
        target = self._find_section(sections, property_name, building_name, unit_name, category)
        if target is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"No section found for property={property_name!r}, "
                f"building={building_name!r}, unit={unit_name!r}, "
                f"category={category!r}"
            )

        original_body = self._extract_body(path, target)
        adjusted_body = self._call_llm(original_body, action, category)
        self._write_back(path, target, adjusted_body)

        return {
            "updated": True,
            "markdown_path": str(path),
            "section_path": " > ".join(target.path),
            "original_content": original_body,
            "adjusted_content": adjusted_body,
        }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Internal helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _resolve_markdown_path(
        self,
        explicit_path: str | Path | None,
        property_name: str,
    ) -> Path:
        if explicit_path is not None:
            path = Path(explicit_path)
            if not path.exists():
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"Markdown file not found: {path}")
            return path

        if not property_name:
            raise ValueError("Either markdown_path or a non-empty property name is required.")

        property_context = self.engine.get_property(property_name)
        if property_context is None:
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"No Markdown file found for property {property_name!r} "
                f"under {self.engine.repo_path}"
            )

        md_path = getattr(property_context, "markdown_path", None)
        if not md_path:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Property {property_name!r} has no markdown_path set.")

        return Path(md_path)

    def _find_section(
        self,
        sections: list[MarkdownSection],
        property_name: str,
        building_name: str,
        unit_name: str,
        category: str,
    ) -> MarkdownSection | None:
        """Return the first section whose path matches all provided components."""
        norm_property = self._normalize(property_name)
        norm_building = self._normalize(building_name)
        norm_unit = self._normalize(unit_name)
        norm_category = self._normalize(category)

        for section in sections:
            path_norm = [self._normalize(p) for p in section.path]

            if norm_category and path_norm[-1] != norm_category:
                continue
            if norm_unit and norm_unit not in path_norm:
                continue
            if norm_building and norm_building not in path_norm:
                continue
            if norm_property and (not path_norm or path_norm[0] != norm_property):
                continue

            return section

        return None

    def _extract_body(self, path: Path, section: MarkdownSection) -> str:
        """Return the section body (lines after the heading) from the file."""
        lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        # start_line is 1-based (heading); body starts at start_line (0-based next line)
        body_lines = lines[section.start_line : section.end_line]
        return "\n".join(body_lines).strip()

    def _call_llm(self, current_content: str, action: str, category: str) -> str:
        """Ask the LLM to apply *action* to *current_content* and return the result."""
        prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages(
            [
                (
                    "system",
                    "You are a property-management document editor. "
                    "You receive the current body of a Markdown section (category: {category}) "
                    "and an action description. "
                    "Apply the action to produce updated content. "
                    "Preserve the existing Markdown list format (lines starting with '- '). "
                    "Return ONLY the updated section body — no headings, no explanations.",
                ),
                (
                    "human",
                    "Current content:\n{content}\n\nAction: {action}\n\nUpdated content:",
                ),
            ]
        )

        chain = prompt | self.llm
        result = chain.invoke(
            {
                "category": category or "section",
                "content": current_content if current_content else "(empty)",
                "action": action,
            }
        )
        return str(result.content).strip()

    def _write_back(self, path: Path, section: MarkdownSection, new_body: str) -> None:
        """Replace the section body in the file, keeping the heading line intact."""
        raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        lines = raw.splitlines(keepends=True)

        # start_line is 1-based; heading is at index start_line-1.
        # Body occupies lines[start_line : end_line] (0-based, exclusive end).
        body_start = section.start_line   # 0-based index of first body line
        body_end = section.end_line       # 0-based exclusive end of body

        new_body_lines: list[str] = []
        if new_body:
            for line in new_body.splitlines():
                new_body_lines.append(line + "\n")
            # Ensure a blank separator before the next section when one follows
            if body_end < len(lines) and new_body_lines and new_body_lines[-1].strip():
                new_body_lines.append("\n")

        updated = lines[:body_start] + new_body_lines + lines[body_end:]
        path.write_text("".join(updated), encoding="utf-8")

    def _normalize(self, value: str) -> str:
        return " ".join(str(value).casefold().strip().strip(":").split())
"}

1. **Resolves the file** — accepts an explicit `markdown_path`, or if omitted uses the `ContextEngine` to locate the file by `property` name under `repo_path`.

5. **Calls the LLM** — sends the current body + `action` description and asks it to return only the updated content (no headings, no commentary), preserving `- item` list format.

6. **Writes back** — splices the new body lines back into exactly the same range, leaving every other line in the file untouched.

Answers user prompts by retrieving relevant sections from property Markdown
files (RAG) and passing them as grounded context to the LLM.
"""

import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from langchain_vendor_a import ChatGooglevendor_a
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate

from context_engine.engine import ContextEngine
from context_engine.markdown_parser import MarkdownParser
from context_engine.models import MarkdownSection

load_dotenv()

_TOP_K = 6       # maximum sections to include in context
_MIN_SCORE = 1   # minimum term-hit score to consider a section relevant
_MIN_TERM_LEN = 3  # ignore query words shorter than this (stop-word heuristic)


class QueryAgent:
    """Answers user prompts about managed properties using RAG."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        api_key: str | None = None,
        repo_path: str | Path = ".",
    ):
        if api_key is None:
            api_key = os.getenv("GOOGLE_<NAME_11>_<NAME_14>")
            if not api_key:
                raise ValueError(
                    "GOOGLE_<NAME_11>_<NAME_14> environment variable not set. "
                    "Please set it or pass api_key parameter."
                )

        self.llm = ChatGooglevendor_a(
            model="<MODEL_A>",
            google_api_key=api_key,
            temperature=0,
        )
        self.parser = MarkdownParser()
        self.engine = ContextEngine(repo_path=repo_path)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public <NAME_11>
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def query(self, prompt: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Answer *prompt* using context retrieved from property Markdown files.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'answer' (str) and 'sources' (list of section paths).
        """
        context_text, sources = self._retrieve_context(prompt)
        answer = self._call_llm(prompt, context_text)
        return {"answer": answer, "sources": sources}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # RAG retrieval
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _retrieve_context(self, query: str) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
        """Return (formatted_context, source_labels) for the top-K sections."""
        terms = [t for t in query.lower().split() if len(t) >= _MIN_TERM_LEN]
        scored: list[tuple[int, MarkdownSection, str]] = []

        for md_path in self.engine._iter_markdown_files():
            try:
                sections = self.parser.parse_file(md_path)
            except Exception:
                continue

            for section in sections:
                content_lower = section.content.lower()
                score = sum(content_lower.count(term) for term in terms)
                if score >= _MIN_SCORE:
                    scored.append((score, section, str(md_path)))

        scored.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
        top = scored[:_TOP_K]

        if not top:
            return "(No relevant property data found for this query.)", []

        context_parts: list[str] = []
        sources: list[str] = []

        for _, section, path in top:
            heading = " > ".join(section.path)
            context_parts.append(f"[{heading}]\n{section.content}")
            sources.append(f"{Path(path).name} — {heading}")

        return "\n\n---\n\n".join(context_parts), sources

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # LLM call
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _call_llm(self, prompt: str, context: str) -> str:
        template = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages(
            [
                (
                    "system",
                    "You are a property management <USER_4> "
                    "Answer the user's question using ONLY the property data "
                    "provided below. "
                    "If the data does not contain enough information to answer, "
                    "say so clearly instead of guessing. "
                    "Be concise and factual.\n\n"
                    "Retrieved property data:\n{context}",
                ),
                ("human", "{prompt}"),
            ]
        )

        chain = template | self.llm
        result = chain.invoke({"context": context, "prompt": prompt})
        return str(result.content).strip()
"}

**`agents/query_agent.py`** — new `QueryAgent` class

- `query(prompt)` → `{"answer": str, "sources": list[str]}`
- **RAG retrieval** (`_retrieve_context`): walks all markdown files via `ContextEngine._iter_markdown_files()`, parses each into sections with `MarkdownParser`, scores every section by counting how many query terms appear in its content, takes the top 6 by score. Short words (< 3 chars) are ignored to avoid stop-word noise.
- **LLM call** (`_call_llm`): passes the ranked sections as grounded context with a system prompt that instructs the model to answer from the data only and say so if it can't — no hallucination.

Answers user prompts by retrieving relevant sections from property Markdown
files (RAG) and passing them as grounded context to the LLM.
"""

import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from langchain_vendor_a import ChatGooglevendor_a
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate

from agents.config import VENDOR_A_MODEL, PROPERTIES_DIR
from context_engine.engine import ContextEngine
from context_engine.markdown_parser import MarkdownParser
from context_engine.models import MarkdownSection

load_dotenv()

_TOP_K = 8          # maximum sections forwarded to the LLM
_MIN_SCORE = 1      # sections scoring below this are discarded
_MIN_TERM_LEN = 3   # query words shorter than this are ignored (stop-word heuristic)
_PATH_WEIGHT = 3    # heading-path hits count this many times more than body hits


class QueryAgent:
    """Answers user prompts about managed properties using RAG."""

    def __init__(self, api_key: str | None = None):
        if api_key is None:
            api_key = os.getenv("GOOGLE_<NAME_11>_<NAME_14>")
            if not api_key:
                raise ValueError(
                    "GOOGLE_<NAME_11>_<NAME_14> environment variable not set. "
                    "Please set it or pass api_key parameter."
                )

        self.llm = ChatGooglevendor_a(
            model=<MODEL_A>,
            google_api_key=api_key,
            temperature=0,
        )
        self.parser = MarkdownParser()
        self.engine = ContextEngine(repo_path=PROPERTIES_DIR)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public <NAME_11>
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def query(self, prompt: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Answer *prompt* using context retrieved from property Markdown files.

        Returns:
            Dict with 'answer' (str) and 'sources' (list of section paths).
        """
        context_text, sources = self._retrieve_context(prompt)
        answer = self._call_llm(prompt, context_text)
        return {"answer": answer, "sources": sources}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # RAG retrieval
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _retrieve_context(self, query: str) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
        """Parse every property file as a section tree, score each leaf section
        against the query, and return the top-K most relevant sections in
        document order.

        Scoring weights heading-path hits (_PATH_WEIGHT × body hits) so that
        structural matches (e.g. a section literally named 'maintenance' when
        the user asks about maintenance) rank above incidental mentions in body
        text.  Sections whose body is empty (pure structural headings) are
        skipped entirely.
        """
        terms = [t for t in query.lower().split() if len(t) >= _MIN_TERM_LEN]
        if not terms:
            return "(Query is too short to search effectively.)", []

        # (score, document_line, section, file_path)
        candidates: list[tuple[int, int, MarkdownSection, Path]] = []

        for md_path in self.engine._iter_markdown_files():
            try:
                sections = self.parser.parse_file(md_path)
            except Exception:
                continue

            for section in sections:
                body = self._body(section)
                if not body:
                    continue  # skip pure structural headings with no content

                path_text = " ".join(section.path).lower()
                path_score = sum(path_text.count(t) for t in terms) * _PATH_WEIGHT
                body_score = sum(body.lower().count(t) for t in terms)
                score = path_score + body_score

                if score >= _MIN_SCORE:
                    candidates.append((score, section.start_line, section, md_path))

        if not candidates:
            return "(No relevant property data found for this query.)", []

        # Select best K by relevance score
        candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
        top = candidates[:_TOP_K]

        # Re-sort into document order so the context reads vendor_ently
        top.sort(key=lambda x: (str(x[3]), x[1]))

        context_parts: list[str] = []
        sources: list[str] = []

        for _, _, section, md_path in top:
            heading = " > ".join(section.path)
            context_parts.append(f"[{heading}]\n{self._body(section)}")
            sources.append(f"{md_path.name} — {heading}")

        return "\n\n---\n\n".join(context_parts), sources

    def _body(self, section: MarkdownSection) -> str:
        """Return section content with the heading line stripped."""
        lines = section.content.splitlines()
        body_lines = lines[1:] if lines and lines[0].startswith("#") else lines
        return "\n".join(body_lines).strip()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # LLM call
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _call_llm(self, prompt: str, context: str) -> str:
        template = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages(
            [
                (
                    "system",
                    "You are a property management <USER_4> "
                    "Answer the user's question using ONLY the property data "
                    "provided below. "
                    "If the data does not contain enough information to answer, "
                    "say so clearly instead of guessing. "
                    "Be concise and factual.\n\n"
                    "Retrieved property data:\n{context}",
                ),
                ("human", "{prompt}"),
            ]
        )

        chain = template | self.llm
        result = chain.invoke({"context": context, "prompt": prompt})
        return str(result.content).strip()
"}

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from context_engine.markdown_parser import MarkdownParser
from context_engine.engine import ContextEngine

md = '''# Riverside
## insurance
- flood coverage active
- fire coverage active
## buildings:
### block-a
#### maintenance
- roof inspection every 2 years
- gutter cleaning annually
#### units:
##### apt-1
###### maintenance
- replace boiler scheduled Q3
###### tenant
Maria Schmidt
###### rent
- 950 EUR per month
##### apt-2
###### tenant
Klaus <USER_5>
###### rent
- 1100 EUR per month
'''

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    Path(d, 'riverside.md').write_text(md)
    engine = ContextEngine(repo_path=d)
    parser = MarkdownParser()

    _PATH_WEIGHT = 3
    _MIN_TERM_LEN = 3
    _MIN_SCORE = 1

    def body(section):
        lines = section.content.splitlines()
        body_lines = lines[1:] if lines and lines[0].startswith('#') else lines
        return '\n'.join(body_lines).strip()

    for query in ['maintenance apt-1', 'all tenants', 'rent block-a']:
        print(f'\n=== {query!r} ===')
        terms = [t for t in query.lower().split() if len(t) >= _MIN_TERM_LEN]
        candidates = []
        for md_path in engine._iter_markdown_files():
            for section in parser.parse_file(md_path):
                b = body(section)
                if not b:
                    continue
                path_score = sum(' '.join(section.path).lower().count(t) for t in terms) * _PATH_WEIGHT
                body_score = sum(b.lower().count(t) for t in terms)
                score = path_score + body_score
                if score >= _MIN_SCORE:
                    candidates.append((score, section.start_line, section))
        candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
        for score, _, s in candidates[:4]:
            print(f'  score={score}  {\" > \".join(s.path)}')
            print(f'    {body(s)[:60]!r}')

Here's what the full hierarchy produces:

| Level | Heading prefix | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| `#` | `# WEG ...` | `PropertyContext.name` |
| `##` | `## insurance` / `## maintanance` / `## buildings:` | `PropertyContext.insurance` / `.maintenance` / `.buildings` |
| `###` | `### building 12` | `PropertyBuildingContext.name` |
| `####` | `#### maintenance` / `#### rent` / `#### units:` | `PropertyBuildingContext.maintenance` / `.rent` / `.units` |
| `#####` | `##### unit WE 01` | `PropertyUnitContext.name` |
| `######` | `###### maintenance` / `###### rent` / `###### tenant` | `PropertyUnitContext.maintenance` / `.rent` / `.tenant` |

Content under each section is read as a list of strings — `- item` bullet points have the `- ` prefix stripped automatically, plain lines are kept as-is. Empty sections (no lines below the heading) come back as `[]` or `""` which is exactly what you have now.

The one thing to note: `#### units:` belongs to the **last building above it** (`### building 16` in your example), not to all buildings. So buildings 12 and 14 have no units, and building 16 gets all 52 units — which matches your structure.
